card.name: Break points inside medical terms
card.fires_on: Marks a point just before or inside a long medical term, often at an opening parenthesis, a first capital letter of an abbreviation, or a syllable break in a dictionary entry. It is most common where a term or its abbreviation is about to be spelled out or repeated.

modes.label: Parenthesis or bracket before a repeated value
modes.description: An opening or closing bracket right after a dose or pronunciation, before the next piece of text.
modes.example: Consider reducing PLUVICTO dose by 20% to 5.9 GBq<< (>>160 mCi).

modes.label: Start of an abbreviation
modes.description: The first letter of an abbreviation such as PD-L1 or DPP-4, written inside the term.

modes.description: A syllable partway through a drug or condition name, often one that is repeated.

card.writes: The promoted tokens are odd word pieces and the suppressed ones are foreign-script pieces, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It fires at spots inside or right before long medical names and abbreviations, such as where a term is spelled out or repeated.
